title: Find a column narrows the Tech View Columns menu without changing ticks
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · about 15 minutes
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011). A desktop browser with the window at least 1024 pixels wide (full screen on an ordinary laptop or monitor). Below that width the page shows only List.
  • [User-A]: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • One technician at this location: [Tech-A] (e.g. "Esther Howard"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Find Column" (used by this case only), with one contact and one asset, so this case's work orders are kept apart from every other work order at the location.
  • One Approved work order for that customer, [WO-1], led by [Tech-A] so [Tech-A]'s group has a row.

Setup

  1. Sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page (you appear as "Admin ShopView"). Check the location in the top bar next to the bell; to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  2. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff > New Staff Member, enter First Name and Last Name (e.g. "Esther Howard") and an email. Pick a Role that is not Office User or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), pick at least one Department (required), set Location to this location and turn Time Clock on, then click Save & Close. Record as [Tech-A].
  3. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Find Column" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  4. Create the work order: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F2 Find Column" and its Asset > Save, and record its number as [WO-1] (e.g. "S1-702"). The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close.
  5. Set the leads: on an Approved work order pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned. Here: [WO-1] = [Tech-A].
  6. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > Search ZZAUTOTEST F2 Find Column > Tech View — [Tech-A]'s group holds [WO-1]. If not, set the lead before starting.
custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders.
  2. Click the All tab.
  3. Type ZZAUTOTEST F2 Find Column in Search.
  4. In the display switcher at the right of the toolbar, click Tech View (tooltip "Tech View").
  5. Write down every column heading in [Tech-A]'s group.
  6. Click the Column Selection button in the toolbar (tooltip "Column Selection").
  7. Write down the count beside the menu heading (e.g. "10 of 10 shown") and every column listed with its tick.
  8. Click the menu's search box (in the design it reads "Find a column") and type ass
  9. Clear the box and type ASS (all capitals).
  10. Clear the box and type zzqx
  11. Clear the box.
  12. Close the Column Selection menu by clicking outside it.
  13. In the display switcher, click Board View (tooltip "Board View").
  14. Click Fields to display in the toolbar (the same place as Column Selection in Tech View).
  15. Type zzqx in its search box, then clear the box.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 8: only the columns whose name contains "ass" stay listed (e.g. "Asset" and "Assigned Techs"). The other columns disappear from the menu but keep their ticks.
  • Step 9: capitals give the same list. Upper or lower case does not matter.
  • Step 10: no column is listed and the menu says nothing matches (in the design: "No columns match"). Write down the words you see; a different wording alone is not a fail.
  • Steps 8 to 10: typing never ticks or unticks anything. The count from step 7 and the column headings from step 5 stay exactly the same.
  • Step 11: clearing the box brings back every column from step 7, each with the same tick.
  • Steps 14 and 15: Fields to display works the same way as the Columns menu: its search box narrows the field list by name, a search that finds nothing says so, and clearing it brings every field back with the same ticks. If Board View has no Fields to display button, mark the case Failed and write "no Fields to display picker" in the comment (the design has none; this is a known difference).

What you should see today (build v26.40.8-7a95011, 10/8/2026): the Tech View "Column Selection" menu and the Board View "Fields to display" menu list their items with ticks and have no search box. (1) If you see exactly that, mark the case Blocked (the developer says this part is not in this release) and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results above say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10048 (Story 5, Fields to display (Board View) and columns (Tech View)); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S2-R4, S5-R2, read 8 Oct 2026. Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Branko Cicovic, Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html) renders the Columns menu through the design system bundle _ds/shopview-design-system-fac6efcf…/_ds_bundle.js: search box "Find a column" (line 552), the menu keeps the columns whose name contains the typed text in any letter case (line 556), no-match text "No columns match" (line 580); ticks are kept separately from the search. Design crawl 8 Oct 2026: Tech View state 123 (Columns > Find a column, typed "Fib" and "zzqx-no-match": "10 of 10 shown | No columns match"). The search box and its wording are design-only details cited to the design; that Board View's Fields to display behaves the same way comes from S5-R2. Board View's missing Fields to display picker in the design is already recorded as a design-vs-spec difference. Source-verified 8 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-R4: “Tech View offers the same columns as List, plus the Assigned Techs column (Story 7), through its own column chooser (Story 5).”
  • S5-R2: “Board View offers a separate Fields to display picker in the same toolbar position and with the same interaction as the column chooser.”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.

AUTOMATION: READY
